core_obligations: Set up the induction on the degree of a finite purely inseparable extension L over K (proof lines 12315-12316).
Settle the base case L = K using regularity of the completion of a regular local ring (proof lines 12317-12318).
Choose an intermediate field M with L obtained by adjoining a p-th root of an element f, and a finite A-subalgebra B of M containing f after clearing denominators (proof lines 12319-12327).
Identify the unique primes over the given prime and rewrite the base change with M as the completed localisation of B, which is regular by induction (proof lines 12328-12336).
Rewrite the base change with L as a quotient of that ring by z^p - f, produce a derivation taking f to a unit, and conclude regularity (proof lines 12337-12353).
proof_roadmap: Induct on the degree of the purely inseparable extension (proof lines 12315-12318).
Adjoin one p-th root and pass to a finite algebra (proof lines 12319-12336).
Use a derivation to satisfy the degree-p regularity criterion (proof lines 12337-12353).
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that the completed localisation of a mixed power series and polynomial algebra over a field of positive characteristic becomes geometrically regular after extending scalars from the fraction field. The proof is an induction on the degree of a finite purely inseparable field extension: the base case is regularity of the completion of a regular local ring, and the induction step adjoins a p-th root, replaces the field by a finite algebra over the base, computes the base change as a quotient of a polynomial ring over a field, and uses a derivation that does not vanish on the element whose p-th root is adjoined. The derivation is extended through localisation and completion, which makes the quotient regular by the degree-p criterion.
